title: Factor Analysis Tool
description: A systematic framework for analyzing how any business combines the four factors of production (land, labor, capital, entrepreneurship) and calculates factor payments and profitability
learning_objectives: Identify all four factors of production in any business context
Calculate factor payments (rent, wages, interest, profit)
Analyze the relative importance of different factors to business success
Understand how efficient factor combination creates value

inputs.label: Business Name
inputs.help_text: Enter the name of the business you want to analyze

inputs.label: Business Type
inputs.help_text: Classify the business into one of these categories

inputs.label: Land/Natural Resources Used
inputs.help_text: Describe the physical location and any natural resources the business uses

inputs.label: Monthly Rent Payment
inputs.help_text: Enter the monthly rent or lease payment for the business location

inputs.label: Labor/Workers Employed
inputs.help_text: Describe the types of workers and their roles

inputs.label: Number of Employees
inputs.help_text: Total number of workers (including owner if working)

inputs.label: Monthly Wages/Payroll
inputs.help_text: Total monthly payroll for all employees

inputs.label: Capital/Equipment Used
inputs.help_text: Describe the major equipment, tools, and machinery the business uses

inputs.label: Total Capital Investment
inputs.help_text: Total value of equipment, machinery, and other capital goods

inputs.label: Monthly Interest/Loan Payments
inputs.help_text: Monthly loan payments for capital equipment (interest portion)

inputs.label: Entrepreneurial Innovation
inputs.help_text: What unique vision, innovation, or risk does the entrepreneur bring?

inputs.label: Initial Investment at Risk
inputs.help_text: How much money did the entrepreneur risk to start this business?

inputs.label: Most Important Factor
inputs.help_text: Which factor is most critical to this business's success?

inputs.label: Explain Your Choice
inputs.help_text: Why is this factor most important for this particular business?

scenarios.name: Downtown Coffee Shop
scenarios.description: A cozy coffee shop in a downtown area

scenarios.name: Software Startup
scenarios.description: A small tech company building a mobile app

validation_rules.condition: monthly_revenue must be greater than 0 for profit calculation
validation_rules.error_message: Please enter monthly revenue to calculate profitability.

validation_rules.condition: At least one factor cost should be greater than 0
validation_rules.error_message: Every business uses at least some factors of production. Enter factor costs.

feedback_messages.profitable: This business is profitable! The entrepreneur earns ${profit} per month as their reward for combining factors effectively and taking risks.
feedback_messages.break_even: This business is at break-even. The entrepreneur isn't earning profit for their risk. Consider ways to increase revenue or reduce costs.
feedback_messages.loss: This business is operating at a loss. The entrepreneur is losing ${loss} per month. Without changes, this business isn't sustainable.
feedback_messages.high_labor: This is a labor-intensive business. Success depends heavily on employee productivity and keeping turnover low.
feedback_messages.high_capital: This is a capital-intensive business. Efficient use of equipment and managing debt are critical to success.
feedback_messages.high_land: Location is critical for this business. The rent reflects the value of being in the right place.
insights: Every business combines the same four factors—the proportions vary by industry
Profit is the entrepreneur's payment for risk-taking and coordination
A business that can't pay competitive wages won't attract good labor
Capital investment increases productivity but requires financing
Location (land) can be the difference between success and failure
